sources: Ship Tuscany left Boston on 12 May 1833 with about 180 tons of ice packed in sawdust; arrived in Calcutta in early September 1833 with about 100 tons still frozen, after about four months. Frederic Tudor ('the Ice King'). American Heritage, 'Cold Mine'; Atlas Obscura, 'How did people get ice'; Scroll.in.

1806, Boston Gazette on Tudor's first ice cargo to Martinique: 'No joke. A vessel with a cargo of 80 tons of Ice has cleared out from this port for Martinique. We hope this will not prove to be a slippery speculation.' (quoted in Smithsonian Magazine / American Heritage). Film: 'S.S. Coptic Sailing Away' (Edison, 1897), public domain, illustrative (Internet Archive).
